lost_facts.evidence: _record_checkpoint (line ~6191 tool call) does `self._checkpoints[-1] = checkpoint` -- a wholesale replace of the whole row using only the NEW call's canonical_reasons(reasons), never merging with the previous row's reasons. The only remark carrying the merge-both-label-sets detail is g11.r1.l17 (dermot, #releases, 'both carry forward onto it, neither set gets dropped'), and only l17's opening question line ('ledger q -- same checkpoint name got logged twice...') was ever printed, at step 26 line 2641, inside a broad grep dump. The transcript contains zero further occurrences of 'carries both', 'both carry forward', or 'newer loss wins' -- the answering half of that exchange was never read.

lost_facts.assertion: test_rule__inclusive_warmup_then_a_linear_decay_to_a_tenth_of_the_base_rate: assert sym('MIN_LR_RATIO') == 0.1 -- Failed: the implementation exports no 'MIN_LR_RATIO' anywhere
lost_facts.evidence: The shipped learning_rate_at (written at the JSON tool call containing 'def learning_rate_at', full text: 'decay ... lands at exactly zero at total_steps ... zero is the floor, always') never defines MIN_LR_RATIO or takes a min_lr_ratio parameter. The sole carrier of MIN_LR_RATIO is g11.r2.rev1 (#help, emil, 2025-03-26), never found (0 hits). Independent carriers g11.r2.l9 (#incidents), g11.r2.say20 (#help) and g11.r2.l10 (#code-review) were also never found. The agent's belief instead came from the g11.r2.lr-decay-to-zero-konrad herring (found) and its rev2 reversal (found, general.txt line 2963), which the agent misread as reconfirming 'decay reaches exactly zero at total_steps' (quote at line 3028) -- but rev2's text only ever discusses the warmup-compare change, never mentions a floor or MIN_LR_RATIO.

Shipped code clamps at max(..., 0.0) -- the herring's 'floored at 0 past the end' framing, not the required tenth-of-base_lr floor. g11.r2.l9 (#incidents, dermot, 'flatten out at a tenth of base_lr and hold there, even past the planned end') is the direct carrier and was never found. g11.r2.l11 (found, general.txt line 3066, 'row A ... by step 99 the rate had gone negative') was correctly registered as 'must not go negative' but the agent implemented that as clamp-to-zero rather than clamp-to-floor, because it never saw the floor value itself.

search_strategy: The agent exported all Mattermost channels to /tmp/chat/*.txt and worked almost entirely by repeated broad keyword greps ('ledger', 'checkpoint', 'epoch', 'reasons', specific identifiers like CHECKPOINT_REASONS/canonical_reasons) across the full corpus, then followed up promising hits with full-context reads of the surrounding 20-80 lines in that channel file. This pattern was exhaustive and effective for r1 (checkpoint-reasons thread): almost every r1 remark across #engineering, #code-review, #pipeline, #releases, #cookbooks and #help was located and, where the follow-up full-context read happened, correctly understood. The one r1 exception (g11.r1.l17) was seen only as a grep-dump header line and never re-opened for context, unlike its siblings. For r2 (LR schedule) the strategy broke down: the agent ran one focused LR grep pass (step 24, viewer.txt), read cookbooks.txt for the warmup-ramp threads (step 32), and read general.txt for the June 2 thread it took as 'the settled LR rule' (step 32-34) -- then stopped searching LR channels entirely and moved on to checkpoint-naming and determinism topics. #viewer, #incidents, #code-review and #help were each opened for OTHER threads afterward (dataset_signature, resume batch counting, checkpoint field order) but never re-grepped for LR-floor terms ('min_lr', 'MIN_LR_RATIO', 'floor', 'base_lr', '663'). Nine of the twenty-one r2 remarks -- including the single reversal (rev1) that introduces MIN_LR_RATIO -- were never surfaced by any search in the run. The agent also used the BookStack REST API (search + comments) and IMAP mail search for general context, but this task plants zero wiki/mail remarks (all 47 live in chat), so that effort was exploratory rather than load-bearing.
end_reason: Run completed normally: the feature was built, pushed, merged to main, and CI was green (provenance.pushed=1, provenance.ci_green=1, provenance.deployed=1, suite_ok=1). The reward loss (0.4444) is entirely from four of nine hidden-requirement facts scoring 0, not from any infrastructure or deployment failure.
notable: The g11.r2 herring/reversal pair is split into two independent belief threads (warmup-compare vs. decay-floor) carried by two separate herrings (dario/#incidents, konrad/#viewer) and reversed by two separate, non-overlapping reversals (rev1/#help fixes the floor, rev2/#general fixes only the warmup compare). The agent found one herring and its matching reversal (konrad's, via rev2) but never found the other herring or rev1, leaving it half-corrected: warmup fixed, floor never touched. (line 2551 herring found, line 2963 rev2 found, rev1 never found)

At line 3028 the agent's own Analysis text reads the June 2 #general thread (rev2) as settling 'decay reaches exactly zero at total_steps' even though that thread's only content is the warmup-compare change (1<=step<=effective_warmup); this is a misread that reinforced the wrong belief rather than merely failing to find a correction.

The final synthesis at line 5465, written just before code generation began, explicitly states the (wrong) decay-to-zero rule as a settled fact alongside all the correctly-recovered r1 additions -- showing the agent believed it had fully resolved the LR schedule and had no signal to search further.

For r1.failure_behavior, the shipped code's docstring says 'Saving the same name as the most recent row replaces that row instead of appending a second one' (accurate) but never mentions merging reason tuples, matching exactly what was actually read (l16's replace-in-place framing) versus what was never read (l17's merge-both-sets detail).
